Bill.BriefDescription: Creating flexible conservation futures taxing districts.

BillBody.BillTitle: AN ACT Relating to creating flexible conservation futures taxingdistricts; and adding a new chapter to Title 36 RCW.
BillBody.EnactingClause: BE IT ENACTED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF THE STATE OF WASHINGTON:

BillSection.RCWSLText: For the purpose of acquiring conservationfutures and other rights and interests in real property pursuant to RCW84.34.210 and 84.34.220, and for maintaining and operating any propertyacquired with these funds, a county may create a flexible conservationfutures taxing district within such county and may enlarge any districtcontaining a lesser territory than the whole county, or reduce anydistrict already created, or combine or consolidate districts ordivide, or create new districts from time to time in the mannerprovided in this chapter.

A levy imposed on property underthis chapter may not exceed a total levy amount of six and onequartercents per thousand dollars of assessed valuation against the assessedvaluation of all taxable property within the county.
For the purposes of thischapter, "district" means a flexible conservation futures taxingdistrict created under this chapter.

SectionCaption.Bold: TAX IN LIEU OF CONSERVATION FUTURES LEVY.

BillSection.RCWSLText: A county may not impose a levy under this chapter on any property onwhich a levy is imposed under RCW 84.34.230.

(1) A district may be initiated upon the adoptionof a resolution of intention by a county legislative authority. Aresolution of intention must set forth: (a) The nature of the district's proposed activities; (b) That the amount of any levies proposed to be raised by thedistrict are in lieu of any conservation futures levies imposed underRCW 84.34.230; and (c) The proposed boundaries of the district. (2) A resolution of intention must also designate the number of theproposed district, and fix a date, time, and place for a public hearingon the formation of the proposed district. The date for the publichearing must be at least thirty days and no more than ninety days afterthe adoption of the resolution of intention unless an emergency exists.

(1) Notice of the public hearing under this chaptermust be published in at least two consecutive issues of a newspaper ofgeneral circulation in the proposed district, the date of the firstpublication to be at least fifteen days prior to the date fixed for thepublic hearing by the resolution of intention. (2) Notices of the public hearing must: (a) Refer to the resolution of intention; (b) Designate the proposed district by number; (c) Set forth a proposed plan describing: (i) The nature of the proposed district activities; and (ii) That the amount of any levies proposed to be raised by thedistrict are in lieu of any conservation futures levies imposed underRCW 84.34.230; and SB 6165 p. 2 (d) Indicate the date, time, and place of the public hearingdesignated in the resolution of intention.

If the countylegislative authority deems the interests of the county or of anyparticular section thereof will be benefited by the creation of adistrict or districts under this chapter, or the changing thereof, itmust make a record thereof upon the minutes of the county legislativeauthority and must designate such territory in each such district as"Flexible Conservation Futures Taxing District No. [insert number] for[insert county name] County."

The county treasurermust be ex officio treasurer for each of the districts formed underthis chapter and the county assessor and other county officers musttake notice of the formation of such district or districts and aregoverned by the provisions of this chapter. The tax levies under thischapter must be extended on the tax rolls against the property liabletherefor the same as other taxes are extended, and must become a partof the general tax against such property and be collected and accountedfor the same as other taxes are, with the terms and penalties attachedthereto. The moneys so collected must be held and disbursed as aspecial fund for such district and must be paid out only on warrantissued by the county auditor upon voucher approved by the board ofcounty commissioners.

The supervisorof the district must be either: (1) The county commissioner within his or her respectivecommissioner district; or (2) A person designated by the county legislative authority, otherthan the county commissioner, to act as the district supervisor. If aperson other than the county commissioner is designated as districtsupervisor, the county legislative authority must fix that person'scompensation therefor. If a county legislative authority member isdesignated as the district supervisor he or she is entitled to his orher actual expenses and his or her per diem as a member of the county p. 3 SB 6165legislative authority, the same as if he or she were doing other countybusiness.
Sections 1 through 9 of this act constitutea new chapter in Title 36 RCW.
